name: Great Revolt against Henry II
summary: Henry II of England's three eldest sons, Henry the Young King, Richard (the future Lionheart), and Geoffrey, rebel simultaneously with the backing of King Louis VII of France, King William I of Scotland, and numerous English barons (1173–1174). The revolt was precipitated by Henry II's refusal to give his sons real power. Scotland invades from the north; rebel barons hold castles across England and Normandy. Henry II's rapid, skillful campaign captures King William of Scotland (1174); the rebellion collapses. Henry II forces his sons to submit at Montlouis, pardons them, but roots out the rebel barons.

_quarry.structural_significance: The most serious dynastic challenge to Henry II; demonstrates the Angevin Empire's internal fragility despite its surface power; the pattern of sons rebelling against their father recurs throughout the Angevin dynasty; Richard's later rebellion (1189) with Philip II finally destroys Henry II
